newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RUGBY UNION-MANU'S TRIES LIFT NSW TO WIN OVER CANTERBURY.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-MANU'S TRIES LIFT NSW TO WIN OVER CANTERBURY.

text.p: Two late tries by substitute flanker Daniel Manu helped New South Wales to their first win in this year's Super 12 tournament as they beat New Zealand side Canterbury 25-8 on Friday.
The home side struggled in the first half to break down a stubborn Canterbury defence and led by only 9-8 at the break thanks to three Matt Burke penalties.

The Wallaby fullback kicked two more penalties to make it 15-8 and when Manu came on as a 58th-minute replacement for test forward Michael Brial the Australians began to take a grip. But they managed to cross the Canterbury line only five minutes from time.

A superb break from world record test try scorer David Campese -- recalled to the NSW team after their 33-26 defeat by Waikato in their opening game -- stretched the visitors' defence and a clever pass put Manu in for the touchdown.

Manu's second try came after the full-time siren in injury time. New South Wales were awarded a penalty just as the siren sounded and, after a fierce forward drive, the Tongan-born flanker barged over the Canterbury line.
Manu, though, was by no means the only hero as the NSW forwards produced a fine all-round effort with number eight Fili Finau standing out as the man of the match.
Scrumhalf Sam Payne was a constant thorn in Canterbury's side while Wallaby fullback Matthew Burke produced a deft kicking display with his five penalties.

Canterbury, who started the match without two All Black players in injured flyhalf Andrew Mehrtens and suspended prop Con Barrell, held the lead briefly in the first half when fullback Daryl Lilley added to his early penalty by darting over for the opening try of the match.

New South Wales - 15-Matthew Burke; 14-David Campese, 13-Graeme Bond, 12-Jason Madz, 11-Alistair Murdoch; 10-Nathan Spooner, 9-Sam Payne; 8-Fili Finau, 7-Stuart Pinkerton, 6-Michael Brial (Daniel Manu 58th minute), 5-Sam Domoni, 4-Tim Gavin (captain), 3-Andrew Blades, 2-Mark Bell, 1-Richard Harry.

Canterbury - 15-Daryl Lilley; 14-James Kerr, 13-Tabai Matson, 12-Mark Mayerhofler, 11-Daryl Gibson; 10-Leon MacDonald, 9-Justin Marshall; 8-Steve Surridge, 7-Scott Robertson, 6-Todd Blackadder (captain), 5-Steve Lancaster, 4-Mark Weedon, 3-Stuart Loe, 2-John Akurangi, 1-Kevin Nepia.
